title: External review: safe shutdown and worker submissions
outcome: Cancellation reaches bounded teardown, wrapper cleanup preserves durable terminal status, and shared checkout workers cannot overwrite or consume another run submission.

tasks.title: Prevent shared-checkout worker submission loss
tasks.body:
## Problem and outcome
External findings: C1.
queueWorkerLifecycle writes one .tusker-worker-lifecycle.json per workspace; consumeWorkerLifecycleRequest validates the embedded request but does not bind it to the run being reconciled. The removed shared-checkout serial guard permits collisions. Restore serial admission for shared-checkout waves and check project, record, attempt and lease generation against the consuming run before applying/removing a request. Preserve isolated workspace concurrency. Per-attempt storage and shared parallelism are explicitly deferred; do not build that larger feature.

## Verified seams and ownership
- `cmd/tusker/armed_wave.go`
- `cmd/tusker/daemon_worker_lifecycle.go`
- `cmd/tusker/daemon_worker_lifecycle_test.go`
- `cmd/tusker/armed_wave_test.go`
Trace the named producer, consumer and every caller before editing. Own only this bounded correction and its focused checks; shared files are not blanket rewrite authority.

## Acceptance
| ID | Required observation |
| --- | --- |
| A1 | Two eligible shared-checkout members never hold overlapping admissions; isolated workspaces still use configured concurrency. |
| A2 | A request for another project/record/attempt/lease generation is neither applied nor removed by the wrong reconciler; its matching owner can still consume it. |
| A3 | A correctly matched acknowledged submission survives reconciliation and follows ordinary terminal/proof/review handling; stale requests cannot close or retry unrelated work. |

## Verification
| Covers | Check | Result | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1,A2,A3 | command: go test ./cmd/tusker -run 'TestExternalReviewSharedSubmission' -count=1 | pending | Add TestExternalReviewSharedSubmission using existing lifecycle fixtures; test both reconciliation orders and admission interleaving. |

## Decisions and boundaries
Keep existing public actions, canonical transitions, project/record identity, ownership, proof and budget checks. Reuse the existing implementation and storage; no parallel scheduler/store/framework. Any deliberate compatibility change beyond the listed defect returns to the operator. The task body and shared context are the handoff; external review text supplies rationale, not permission to expand scope.

tasks.title: Make ACP cancellation and teardown bounded under blocked I/O
tasks.body:
## Problem and outcome
External findings: B1,B2.
respondPermission holds state.mu during writeAll; Cancel/Close/poison need that state lock before closing transport. Close also awaits processDone without a bounded stderr drain. Linearize the permission decision without retaining cancellation-visible locks across blocking I/O. Bound post-exit pipe drain with exec.Cmd.WaitDelay or the existing owned transport lifecycle, while leaving prompt duration unlimited.

## Verified seams and ownership
- `internal/acp/client.go`
- `internal/acp/client_test.go`
Trace the named producer, consumer and every caller before editing. Own only this bounded correction and its focused checks; shared files are not blanket rewrite authority.

## Acceptance
| ID | Required observation |
| --- | --- |
| A1 | A blocked permission-response write cannot prevent Cancel, Close or poison from reaching transport teardown within configured cleanup bounds; no duplicate response or post-cancel unauthorized selection is emitted. |
| A2 | An adapter descendant retaining stderr cannot hang initialization-failure or explicit-interruption cleanup; direct process wait and reader cleanup return. |
| A3 | A quiet unfinished prompt remains active with prompt/stall deadlines disabled, and explicit cancellation still terminates it within cleanup bounds. |

## Verification
| Covers | Check | Result | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1,A2,A3 | command: go test ./internal/acp -run 'TestExternalReviewTeardown' -count=1 | pending | Add deterministic blocked permission write, retained stderr, startup failure and quiet-prompt regressions; do not merely inspect config defaults. |

## Decisions and boundaries
Keep existing public actions, canonical transitions, project/record identity, ownership, proof and budget checks. Reuse the existing implementation and storage; no parallel scheduler/store/framework. Any deliberate compatibility change beyond the listed defect returns to the operator. The task body and shared context are the handoff; external review text supplies rationale, not permission to expand scope.

tasks.title: Publish terminal status before contained runner cleanup
tasks.body:
## Problem and outcome
External findings: B3.
monitorBoundedRunnerCommand can SIGKILL the wrapper-owned group on ErrWaitDelay before status publication; overflow only kills the direct child and post-status cleanup is ACP-only. Keep wrapper-contained monitor cleanup from killing its own status publisher. Extend wrapper-owned post-status containment cleanup to non-ACP runners. Preserve separate uncontained behavior and stale-PGID safeguards. Consume the bounded ACP teardown from predecessor when exercising wrapper interruption.

## Verified seams and ownership
- `cmd/tusker/runner_raw_log_limit.go`
- `cmd/tusker/runner_wrapper.go`
- `cmd/tusker/runner_raw_log_limit_test.go`
- `cmd/tusker/runner_wrapper_test.go`
Trace the named producer, consumer and every caller before editing. Own only this bounded correction and its focused checks; shared files are not blanket rewrite authority.

## Acceptance
| ID | Required observation |
| --- | --- |
| A1 | In a real wrapper-owned group, root exit with inherited pipes, overflow and cancellation each leave a durable truthful terminal record before group teardown. |
| A2 | All descendants in the still-owned contained group are gone after cleanup; uncontained commands retain their existing safe cleanup behavior. |
| A3 | Repeated cleanup/status publication cannot overwrite a known terminal result or signal an unrelated/reused process group. |

## Verification
| Covers | Check | Result | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1,A2,A3 | command: go test ./cmd/tusker -run 'TestExternalReviewContainment' -count=1 | pending | Add TestExternalReviewContainment using wrapper fixtures, not a standalone child-only harness. |

## Decisions and boundaries
Keep existing public actions, canonical transitions, project/record identity, ownership, proof and budget checks. Reuse the existing implementation and storage; no parallel scheduler/store/framework. Any deliberate compatibility change beyond the listed defect returns to the operator. The task body and shared context are the handoff; external review text supplies rationale, not permission to expand scope.
